10590.html:
10590 ráṭati 'cries, yells' Kāv. 2. *raṭyati. [√raṭ]
    1. Pa. raṭati 'screams'; Pk. raḍaï 'calls out', S. raṛaṇu; L. raṛaṇ 'to grunt (of camel)'; Or. raṛibā 'to caw, wail'; OAw. raraï 'wails'; H. (poet.) rarnā 'to shout'; G. raṛvũ 'to weep', M. raḍṇẽ, laḍṇẽ, Ko. raḍtā; — ext. -kk-: S. raṛkaṇu 'to eat noisily', raṛko m. 'cry'; — -ḍ-: L. (Ju.) raṛṛaṇ 'to cry out'.
    2. H. raṭnā 'to cry out, repeat', roā-rāṭ m. 'lamentation' (metath. in ṭarrānā 'to scream'?).
    Addenda: ráṭati. 3. †*rāṭayati (raṭayati 'howls' Daś.): WPah.kṭg. raṛnõ 'to chop (branches off a tree)' — cf. Sk. raṭati 'crashes (as axe on tree)' Prab. (Him.I 185).

10591.html:
10591 raṭana n. 'shouting' Rājat. [√raṭ]
    Pk. raḍaṇa- n. 'crying'; M. raḍṇẽ n. 'crying, weeping'.
